newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 12.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
London's Deutsche Morgan Grenfell investment bank is expected to disclose that despite reported losses at the bank, many senior managers received multi-million pound bonuses last year.
-- EUROTUNNEL TO RELAUNCH FREIGHT SHUTTLE SERVICE

In its first moves to resume freight shuttle service since the fire on November 18th of last year, Eurotunnel officials have announced they are to begin 'experimental' freight shuttle service on Wednesday. Eurotunnel has invited road hauliers to send their lorries through the tunnel at no charge pending approval by the Anglo- French safety authority of the new open lattice design for truck carriers which the UK fire service has condemned.
-- CITY BANKS ATTACK EU PLAN TO LIMIT PHONE CALL TAPING

The London Investment Bankers Association is protesting against planned EU measures on telephone taping which they fear will negatively affect their routine taping of trader phone calls. Investment banks tape calls without prior consent in case of disagreements between traders and customers over transactions. The new EU measures would forbid anonymous taping of any individual without permission. The Confederation of British Industry and The Department of Trade and Industry have declared support for the Liba protest.
-- PLAN TO DEFUSE MILLENNIUM BOMB LAUNCHED

On Monday, the UK government will launch initiatives into dealing with the millennium bomb problem, whereby computers cannot recognize dates beyond 1999. The six-volume set of guides being released cover all areas of starting, managing and successfully implementing year 2000 compliance programmes, and are believed to be the first such guides in the world.
-- HEADHUNTER BRINGS SILICON VALLEY TO EUROPE

Headhunting firm Greenfield Ventures is offering its 'Silicon Valley' -type services to promising ventures in the UK in exchange for equity. The method of company formation is common in the US but new to Europe and allows companies early in development to obtain a variety of services such as legal advice and executive search without taking money from cash reserves.
-- PRIVATE THOUGHTS ON BBC RADIO SALE

The Commercial Radio Companies association is tendering a study into ways of boosting long-term development of radio, which includes an examination of the commercial sector revenue effects of privatising BBC Radios 1 and 2. Sector executives believe that even with the extra competition brought about by privatisation of BBC radio stations, long-term benefits would ensue through the growth in importance of commercial radio as an advertising medium.
-- CO-OP LOOKS TO LAW FOR SAFETY

The Co-operative movement has thrown away plans to change its structuring and has announced it will now seek changes in the law to help keep away any further predatory bidders. Co-op last week passed onto the government a bill which reportedly made a case "for a long overdue reform", demanding the 39-year old Industrial and Provident Act be replaced as it does not suit co-operatives.
-- PHARMACIA & UPJOHN APPOINTS NEW CHIEF EXECUTIVE

The US-Swedish pharmaceuticals group Pharmacia & Upjohn has appointed Fred Hassan as its new chief executive. Hassan was the former senior executive at US drugs company American Home Products, and will attempt to help along the P&U merger between the two countries which began in 1995. Interim chief-executive Jan Ekberg will resume his position as non-executive chairman.
-- FTSE ALL-SHARE INDEX TO BE CALCULATED EVERY MINUTE

Beginning at 12:00pm on Monday, the UK's FTSE All-Share Index will be updated every minute of the trading day as opposed to the current updates once at the end of each trading day. FTSE, owned by the Financial Times and the London Stock Exchange, has made the move to respond to increasing demand for monitoring portfolio risk throughout the day. The All-Share Index covers approximately 98 per cent of all UK quoted stocks and equities. BMC +44-171-377-1742
